header.title_plain: Slow-twitch muscle refuels twice as fast and has twice the aerobic capacity of fast-twitch — and the two are controlled differently

citation.authors: Kushmerick MJ, Meyer RA, Brown TR

header.evidence_type: Ex-vivo animal study (cat muscles, isolated and artificially perfused), 31P-NMR plus oxygen measurements. n = 4 + 3 muscles (NMR), 7 + 7 (oxygen).

confidence.why: Capped at moderate because this is an ex-vivo animal study (isolated, perfused cat muscle); moderate for the mechanism, not transferable as a prescription.

practical_relevance.why: A mechanism paper that explains why fibre types behave differently; nothing here changes what a coach programs.

who.name: Cat biceps brachii
who.other: Fibre type: fast-twitch (FG + FOG). Preparation: isolated, perfused with red cells, 30 °C.

who.name: Cat soleus
who.other: Fibre type: slow-twitch (SO, ~100%). Preparation: same (isolated, perfused with red cells, 30 °C).

conditions.name: Twitch stimulation
conditions.description: Electrical twitch stimulation; each muscle tested at 2–4 rates.
conditions.other: Measured: oxygen uptake at steady state, PCr, Pi, ATP and pH by NMR; ADP calculated from the creatine-kinase equilibrium.

comparison.design_notes: Ex-vivo preparation: cat biceps brachii and soleus isolated and perfused with red cells at 30 °C; 31P-NMR plus oxygen measurements. Electrical twitch stimulation at 0.05–2 Hz for 15–20 min, then ≥1 h recovery; each muscle tested at 2–4 rates. Measured: oxygen uptake at steady state, PCr, Pi, ATP and pH by NMR; ADP calculated from the creatine-kinase equilibrium. Conclusion drawn: simple ADP feedback explains the fast-twitch muscle; it is "not sufficient" for the slow-twitch muscle, which shows an unexplained overshoot during recovery.

measured.note: Cited value, not measured in this study.

layer2.what_it_means: Slow-twitch muscle isn't just "more enduring" in a vague sense: in this preparation it had about twice the oxygen-using capacity, recovered its phosphocreatine in less than half the time (half-time ~4 min vs ~10 min), and barely acidified at workloads that made fast-twitch muscle acidic. That's the physiological basis for the common observation that slow-twitch-dominant athletes recover between efforts quickly and tolerate high-frequency work, and that fast-twitch-dominant athletes need longer rests. It also warns that whole-muscle measurements in humans blend both fibre types, so an individual's recovery curve depends on their fibre mix.
layer2.what_it_doesnt_mean: It's cat muscle, removed from the body and perfused in a magnet at 30 °C, with three or four muscles per group. Twitch stimulation at up to 2 Hz is nothing like a lift or a sprint. The paper is about how respiration is regulated, not about training; the numbers above should not be quoted as human values. The authors themselves end by warning against "simplistic mechanistic interpretations."

translation: Slow-twitch muscle: ~2× the aerobic capacity, PCr refilled in ~4 min half-time vs ~10 min for fast-twitch (in this animal preparation).
Fast-twitch muscle acidifies under repeated work; slow-twitch barely does.

glossary_candidates.definition: What's released when PCr or ATP is spent; rises during work and is linked to fatigue.
How long it takes to refill half the spent phosphocreatine after effort — a marker of mitochondrial capacity and a guide to rest intervals.
A tissue removed from the animal and kept alive artificially so it can be measured precisely; precise, but not the same as a living body.
A simple exponential recovery — the same fraction restored each minute.
